overview: The two mechanisms cells use to generate ATP, distinguished by whether the electron transport chain is involved.
genZNote: Substrate-level phosphorylation: ATP made by hand. Oxidative phosphorylation: ATP made by the electron transport chain's assembly line.

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: ATP synthesis driven by the proton gradient generated by the electron transport chain, via ATP synthase.
aspects.valueB: ATP synthesis by direct transfer of a phosphate group from a high-energy intermediate to ADP.

aspects.label: Mechanism
aspects.valueA: Electrons pass through the electron transport chain, pumping protons; ATP synthase uses the gradient (chemiosmosis) to make ATP.
aspects.valueB: A phosphorylated intermediate (e.g. 1,3-bisphosphoglycerate, phosphoenolpyruvate) directly donates its phosphate to ADP.

aspects.label: Oxygen Requirement
aspects.valueA: Requires oxygen (or another final electron acceptor) as the terminal step of the electron transport chain.
aspects.valueB: Does not require oxygen — occurs in both aerobic and anaerobic pathways.

aspects.label: Occurs In
aspects.valueA: Inner mitochondrial membrane (or plasma membrane in prokaryotes).
aspects.valueB: Cytoplasm during glycolysis and in the citric acid cycle (succinyl-CoA synthetase step).

aspects.label: ATP Yield
aspects.valueA: The majority of ATP produced from glucose oxidation (~26-28 of ~30-32 ATP).
aspects.valueB: A small, direct contribution — 2 ATP net from glycolysis, plus 2 GTP/ATP from the citric acid cycle.

aspects.label: Key Distinguishing Feature
aspects.valueA: ATP made via the electron transport chain and chemiosmosis; requires oxygen.
aspects.valueB: ATP made by direct phosphate transfer; oxygen-independent.
